source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Care is organized mainly around isolated acute visits, with limited responsibility for coordination across clinicians, settings, or periods between appointments.","B":"Care decisions are directed primarily by clinicians without incorporating patient preferences, because standardization takes priority over individualized goals.","C":"Care is comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, usually through an ongoing team-based primary care approach.","D":"Care is delivered only during inpatient admissions, because the medical-home model is designed for hospital-based management rather than longitudinal primary care."}}
source_row.rationale: AHRQ defines the patient-centered medical home as comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, with team-based care supporting those functions. Option C includes these defining attributes. Option A reduces the model to disconnected episodic care. Option B removes patient preferences from decision-making. Option D incorrectly limits the medical-home model to inpatient care rather than longitudinal primary care.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ — Defining the Patient-Centered Medical Home: five core attributes are comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and quality and safety, typically supported by team-based primary care. Current AHRQ PCMH definition at cited federal URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, continuity, confidentiality, quality/cost-effective care, legal/ethical rights and assignment/delegation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
